BiblicalUsage: mâshôwṭ is an oar, and it occurs twice, both times in the lament over Tyre. In Ezekiel 27:6 the oars of Tyre are made of the oaks of Bashan, and in Ezekiel 27:29 all who handle the oar, the mariners and the pilots of the sea, come down from their ships and stand upon the land. The word is the oar laid down in ruin.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mâshôwṭ shows me that even the rowers of Tyre must come down from their ships, and that the sea gives no safety from God.
